description: The human governance CORE: a Directory of human principals, human roles as (subject, role, scope) with a scope hierarchy, a role/capability matrix, PULL-BASED principal-state enforcement (a suspended human's next action fails closed), an org-wide kill switch, and a versioned admin audit log threaded by a correlation id — all as pure enforcement code in services/amazai/ with no AWS calls, mirroring the existing policy.py/agents.py/identity.py conventions. This is the blueprint's MVP admin layer (SSO+roles already exist via Auth0; this adds roles/invite-state/offboard-as-suspension, org ask-first governance surface, and admin audit). It builds ON the existing enforcement chokepoint rather than rebuilding it. No handler wiring in this feature — that is FEAT-003 — so this stays a self-contained, unit-tested module set.
steps: Add key builders in services/amazai/keys.py for the new entities, matching the shapes documented in docs/architecture/03-data-model.md § 'The multi-user seam' and the existing key style (single source of truth, zero-padded/ordered suffixes where ordering matters): org_pk(org_id)->'ORG#<orgId>'; member_sk(subject)->'MEMBER#<subject>'; and an admin-audit key using an ordered suffix so entries sort chronologically under the org partition (e.g. org_pk(org_id) with sk 'ADMINAUDIT#<iso>#<ordered_suffix()>'). Reuse store.ordered_suffix() exactly as agents.audit_event does. Do not introduce a second table or a GSI change.

Create services/amazai/directory.py: the human Directory + RBAC engine. Define Role as a str Enum with EXACTLY the blueprint's six roles: OWNER='owner', ADMIN='admin', SECURITY='security', BILLING='billing', MEMBER='member', AUDITOR='auditor' (Read-only Auditor). Define Scope as a str Enum with the hierarchy PLATFORM='platform' > ORG='org' > WORKSPACE='workspace' > BOT='bot' (only ORG is ever written in v1, but model the tuple (subject, role, scope, scope_id) now so workspaces later are a feature not a migration — per docs/architecture/03-data-model.md). Define MemberState as a str Enum: INVITED='invited', ACTIVE='active', SUSPENDED='suspended'. Provide: a capability matrix mapping each Role to the set of admin capabilities it holds, transcribed EXACTLY from the blueprint §§4 roles matrix (invite_users, change_org_policies, enforce_auto_review, terminate_computer, see_all_usage, manage_payment, impersonate, read_audit_log, create_bot_templates, use_member_app); a Membership dataclass(frozen) carrying subject, role, scope, scope_id, state; can(membership, capability)->bool that returns False for any non-ACTIVE member (pull-based: a suspended/invited principal holds NO capabilities); assert_can(membership, capability) raising an Escalation-style error otherwise. Reuse agents.Escalation (or a directory-local subclass of PermissionError) and agents.ValidationError so HTTP mapping in api.py already works. Include pure row-builders (invite_member/member_row/suspend patch/reactivate patch) that RETURN dicts for the caller to store (same pattern as agents.audit_event and agents.plan_create), never touching the store directly. Keep the Owner role special: exactly one non-removable Owner; suspending or demoting the last Owner must raise ValidationError.

Create services/amazai/govern.py (or extend policy.py — prefer a new module to keep policy.py's floor logic untouched): the org-wide kill switch and the principal-state gate that threads into the enforcement chokepoint. Provide a KillSwitch row-builder + a pure predicate frozen()/is_frozen(row) and a Decision-style guard assert_not_frozen(killswitch_row) that raises a PermissionError when the org is frozen (fail closed: a missing/None row means NOT frozen, an explicitly frozen row blocks). Provide guard_principal(membership) that fails closed when the acting human is not ACTIVE — this is the pull-based offboarding cut: enforcement re-checks principal state on each action so an in-flight routine belonging to a suspended human dies on its next gated action. Add a versioned admin-audit envelope builder admin_audit_event(org_id, action, actor, *, correlation_id=None, before=None, after=None, detail='') that returns an append-only row with an explicit schema/envelope version field (e.g. 'v':1) and a correlationId so 'who approved this external send' is one query joining admin audit to the existing per-run evidence bundle. The correlation id must be OPTIONAL-in, ALWAYS-out (generate one via store.new_id('corr_') when not supplied). Enumerate the admin actions in an ADMIN_AUDITED_ACTIONS tuple exactly like agents.AUDITED_ACTIONS (e.g. member.invited, member.suspended, member.reactivated, member.role_changed, org.policy_changed, org.frozen, org.unfrozen, harness.terminated, connector.revoked_by_admin, impersonation.started, impersonation.ended). Keep this module free of AWS calls.

Extend services/amazai/identity.py minimally to expose the membership seam WITHOUT breaking the single-owner default: add a helper (e.g. load_membership(store, principal) or a Principal.org_id note) that, when no MEMBER# rows exist, returns an implicit ACTIVE OWNER membership for the sole owner — preserving today's 'one workspace per owner' behaviour — and otherwise returns the stored membership. Do NOT change identity.verify or assert_owner semantics; the token-derived subject rule is inviolate. Add a note comment pointing at docs/architecture/03-data-model.md § multi-user seam.

Write tests: tests/test_directory.py — the role/capability matrix matches the blueprint §§4 exactly (parametrized over every (role, capability) cell, asserting both allowed and denied cells); a SUSPENDED or INVITED member holds zero capabilities regardless of role (pull-based fail-closed); the last Owner cannot be suspended or demoted (ValidationError); scope tuple round-trips through the row-builders; can() vs assert_can() agree. tests/test_govern.py — assert_not_frozen blocks when frozen and passes when the row is missing/None (fail-closed on freeze, open by default); guard_principal blocks a non-ACTIVE principal and passes an ACTIVE one; admin_audit_event always emits a correlationId (generated when absent, preserved when supplied) and carries the envelope version and only ADMIN_AUDITED_ACTIONS are accepted; the row is shaped for append-only chronological ordering under the org partition. Use the moto `store`/`table` fixtures from tests/conftest.py for any row that is actually persisted, and pure-function assertions for the builders/predicates. Each test must fail if the behaviour it guards is reverted (the existing suite has caught real bugs — that is the bar).
acceptance_criteria: services/amazai/directory.py defines exactly the six roles owner/admin/security/billing/member/auditor and a capability matrix whose cells match the blueprint §4 roles matrix
A non-ACTIVE (suspended or invited) membership returns False from can() for every capability, and the last Owner cannot be suspended or demoted (raises ValidationError)
govern.assert_not_frozen fails closed when the kill switch row is frozen and passes when it is missing/None; guard_principal fails closed for a non-ACTIVE principal
admin_audit_event always returns a row carrying a correlationId (generated if not supplied), an envelope version field, and rejects any action outside ADMIN_AUDITED_ACTIONS
identity still returns an implicit ACTIVE Owner membership when no MEMBER# rows exist (single-owner behaviour unchanged) and identity.verify/assert_owner are semantically unchanged
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q shows the new tests passing and no NEW failures beyond the 3 pre-existing test_gaps_api.py ones
verification: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_directory.py tests/test_govern.py tests/test_identity.py tests/test_policy.py tests/test_agents.py -q
findings: Implemented the human governance core as pure enforcement code in services/amazai/ (no AWS calls), no handler wiring (that is FEAT-003). Delivered: (1) keys.py builders org_pk/member_sk/admin_audit_sk, reusing store.ordered_suffix() for the ADMINAUDIT# sort key, single table, no GSI change. (2) directory.py with Role/Scope/MemberState str Enums, a Capability enum, the CAPABILITIES matrix transcribed EXACTLY from the blueprint roles matrix, frozen Membership dataclass, can()/assert_can() (non-ACTIVE members hold zero capabilities; assert_can raises agents.Escalation), row builders invite_member/member_row/membership_of/suspend_patch/reactivate_patch/change_role_patch, and the last-Owner floor (suspend or demote of the last ACTIVE owner raises agents.ValidationError; a suspended owner does not count toward the floor). (3) govern.py with killswitch_row/is_frozen/assert_not_frozen (fail-closed: missing/None row => NOT frozen; explicit frozen row raises Frozen), guard_principal (raises PrincipalNotActive for non-ACTIVE), and admin_audit_event with AUDIT_ENVELOPE_VERSION=1, correlationId optional-in/always-out via store.new_id('corr_'), gated by ADMIN_AUDITED_ACTIONS. (4) identity.load_membership returning an implicit ACTIVE OWNER membership when no MEMBER# rows exist, stored row otherwise; verify/assert_owner left semantically unchanged (lazy import of directory to avoid an import cycle). Tests: tests/test_directory.py (matrix parametrized over every role/capability cell against an independently-transcribed EXPECTED table, non-ACTIVE fail-closed, last-Owner floor, scope round-trip, can/assert_can agreement, owner-isolated persisted row) and tests/test_govern.py (freeze fail-closed/open-by-default, principal cut, correlationId generated/preserved, envelope version, action gating, chronological append-only shape, persisted-row query), plus a TestMembershipSeam in tests/test_identity.py. Verification: the two commands in the verification array pass (feature set green), and full suite is 955 passed / 3 failed. The 3 failures are the documented PRE-EXISTING tests/test_gaps_api.py toolchain-drift failures (test_activity_after_the_marker_makes_it_unread_again, test_only_actual_files_are_listed_not_sealed_runs, test_files_are_newest_first) — no NEW failures introduced. Committed on branch main (source + tests staged by name; tracked __pycache__ .pyc changes deliberately not staged).
